jobs.title: Senior Program Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT JUNIPER SQUARE

Private markets are one of the largest, most complex, and most underserved corners of global finance. Our mission at Juniper Square is to unlock their full potential. We’re the Operations Partner trusted by 2,300+ GPs, unifying technology, data, and fund administration services into a single platform that helps GPs move faster, make better decisions, and scale with precision. With $300B+ under administration and 700,000+ LPs on platform, we’ve built the scale to match our ambition. And with JunieAI, our purpose-built AI platform, we’re reimagining how private markets operate, embedding intelligence across every workflow. Founder-led since 2014, backed by $350M+ in funding, and now 1,000+ employees strong, we’re building a company designed to shape the future of private markets for decades to come.

Our culture is built for people who want to do ambitious, meaningful work alongside exceptionally talented teammates. We think like owners, move with urgency, and take pride in solving hard problems that truly matter to our customers and the future of private markets. We believe the best ideas come from open debate, deep collaboration, and diverse perspectives, which is why we believe transparency is the default and feedback makes us stronger. If you’re energized by high standards, rapid growth, and the opportunity to help define a category at a pivotal moment, come join us!

Juniper Square offers employees a variety of ways to work, ranging from a fully remote experience to working full-time in one of our physical offices. We invest heavily in digital-first https://blog.junipersquare.com/juniper-square-ponders-future-of-office-with-digital-first-hybrid-workplace-strategy/ operations, allowing our teams to collaborate effectively across 27 U.S. states, 2 Canadian Provinces, India, Luxembourg, and England. We also have physical offices in San Francisco, New York City, Mumbai and Bangalore for employees who prefer to work in an office some or all of the time.




ABOUT YOUR ROLE

As a Senior Program Manager, PMO, you will own program management for Juniper Square’s most complex, cross-functional software initiatives, driving execution from planning through release while acting as a senior voice inside our Program Management Office (PMO). You will partner closely with engineering, product, design, QA, platform, and operations leadership to build program plans, resolve dependencies, and keep delivery on track against customer commitments. You will act as a bridge between engineering, product management, and other cross-functional partners, translating ambiguous, high-stakes problems into a program plan that accounts for internal and external dependencies.

Beyond your own programs, you will help set the standard for how the PMO runs: contributing to governance, process standardization, metrics, and, critically, how the team uses AI. This role carries a heavy AI focus. You are expected to operate at the Workflow Orchestrator level on Juniper Square’s AI fluency ladder. That means you do not just use AI tools yourself; you design and deploy multi-step workflows that span multiple tools or data sources and replace manual coordination, and you build the reusable systems (prompt libraries, Cowork skills and plugins, scripted Jira/Confluence data extraction) that other program and technical program managers across the org rely on. You will be looked to as the AI thought leader for the PMO organization, actively raising the AI fluency floor for the team.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own program management for Juniper Square’s most complex, multi-team software initiatives, partnering with engineering, product, design, QA, platform, and operations to build program plans, resolve cross-functional dependencies, and drive execution through every stage of the software development lifecycle.

 - Act as a senior bridge between engineering and product management, translating ambiguous, cross-functional problems into a concrete program plan with clear milestones, owners, and dependencies, including with third-party teams where relevant.

 - Establish and evolve the execution framework (agile/scrum ceremonies, artifacts, governance cadence) for your programs, and contribute those improvements back into PMO-wide standards and processes.

 - Provide regular, senior-leadership-ready status reporting; proactively identify, monitor, and mitigate risk; apply change management discipline when scope or timelines shift.

 - Contribute to PMO governance, including metrics definitions, process standardization, and adherence tracking, across the broader program management team.

 - Design and deploy multi-step, AI-powered workflows, such as Cowork skills and plugins and scripted Jira/Confluence extraction and analysis, that replace manual PMO coordination, built as systems other PMs and TPMs can reuse rather than one-off personal shortcuts.

 - Maintain a working library of reusable prompts, templates, and automations for high-frequency PMO work (status reporting, metrics dashboards, roadmap artifacts) and proactively share them across the team.

 - Serve as an AI thought leader for the PMO org: define what “good” looks like before automating a workflow, build in validation steps, and own the accuracy of anything you ship. You can delegate the work, never the accountability.

 - Mentor and coach TPMs and PMs on day-to-day program management practice, PMO goals, and their own AI fluency; contribute to roadmap planning and help anticipate delivery challenges across the organization.

 - Ensure program documentation, status reporting, and delivery metrics are maintained on a regular, reliable cadence.
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.

 - 15+ years of total industry experience, including 8+ years of technical program management on complex, large programs spanning multiple cross-functional teams.

 - Deep understanding of the product development lifecycle and technical program management at scale, with a track record of driving programs from concept through release across multiple teams.

 - Demonstrated AI fluency at the Workflow Orchestrator level: you have designed and deployed at least one multi-step AI or Cowork workflow spanning multiple tools or data sources, with a measurable time or quality improvement you can speak to specifically. Not just personal, ad hoc prompting.

 - Comfortable maintaining a working library of reusable prompts, skills, or workflow templates, and configuring Cowork skills, connectors, and plugins without needing engineering support.

 - Hands-on experience automating program-management workflows with AI, for example scripting or using AI tools to extract and analyze data from Jira and Confluence, generate status reports, or build reusable prompt libraries and templates that others rely on.

 - Comfort defining quality criteria before deploying AI-assisted workflows, validating outputs, and owning the accuracy of anything you automate.

 - Experience with project management tooling (Atlassian suite, Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or equivalent) and Agile/Scrum; working familiarity with SAFe.

 - Experience partnering cross-functionally with product management, design and UX, customer success, customer support, and other functions such as sales, marketing, and legal as needed.

 - Experience with program and project governance: budgeting, vendor management, compliance, and metrics.

 - Professional credentials (PMI PMP, ACP, CSM) a plus.

 - Experience with fintech platforms, cloud platforms (AWS), Docker, and Kubernetes a plus.

 - Self-driven and adaptable, comfortable mentoring peers, and flexible working with counterparts across geographies and time zones.
   
   


COMPENSATION

Compensation for this position includes a base salary and equity, and a variety of benefits. The U.S. base salary range for this role is $150,000 to $190,000 USD. The Canadian base salary range for this role is $120,000 to $150,000 CAD. Actual base salaries will be based on candidate-specific factors, including experience, skillset, and location, and local minimum pay requirements as applicable.



Benefits include:

 - Health, dental, and vision care for you and your family

 - Life insurance

 - Mental wellness coverage

 - Fertility and growing family support

 - Flex Time Off in addition to company-paid holidays

 - Paid family leave, medical leave, and bereavement leave policies

 - Retirement saving plans

 - Allowance to customize your work and technology setup at home

 - Annual professional development stipend

Your recruiter can provide additional details about compensation and benefits.

ABOUT YOUR ROLE

Juniper Square’s Revenue Operations team is the operational backbone of our go-to-market motion. As our Senior Revenue Operations Manager, Fund Administration, you’ll serve as the dedicated Revenue Operations partner for our Fund Administration business. You'll own the systems, processes, and reporting that keep Fund Administration, Sales, Customer Success, and Finance aligned and moving fast, from CRM health and renewal/forecasting workflows to pipeline reviews and cross-functional reporting cadences. You’ll report to the Senior Manager, Revenue Operations, and partner closely with Fund Administration, Sales, Customer Success, and Finance leadership.



What you’ll do

 - Serve as the primary Revenue Operations partner for the Fund Administration business, ensuring alignment on priorities, strategies, and execution plans, and acting as the operational glue between Fund Administration and other departments.

 - Own the health and integrity of our Salesforce (CRM) instance — data quality, workflow configuration, and process governance across Fund Administration and the broader RevOps funnel.

 - Own and optimize the end-to-end renewal workflow process, ensuring efficiency, accuracy, and scalability, and maintaining clear documentation of timelines, responsibilities, and required actions.

 - Manage the forecasting process for Fund Administration and broader RevOps, including pipeline reviews, forecast roll-ups, and reporting cadences, integrating key metrics such as renewals, upsells, and churn.

 - Design, document, and continuously improve revenue processes (e.g., lead routing, opportunity management, territory and quota administration, and a standardized expansion deal process) to remove friction.

 - Build and maintain dashboards and reporting that give a clear, accurate view of pipeline, conversion, renewals, and revenue performance.

 - Establish and enforce clear rules of engagement for Fund Administration's interactions with other departments, serving as a point of escalation for cross-functional disputes and ensuring smooth handoffs and alignment.

 - Partner cross-functionally with Fund Administration, Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Finance to align on shared metrics, definitions, and operating rhythms (QBRs, pipeline reviews, forecast calls).

 - Use AI tools (e.g., Claude) to orchestrate multi-step workflows that reduce manual work across recurring RevOps tasks.

 - Identify and prioritize opportunities for process automation and tooling improvements across the revenue tech stack, and support change management and enablement for new tools and processes.

 - Support pricing and packaging, sales compensation, territory design, and quota-setting processes in partnership with Fund Administration and Sales leadership and Finance.

Qualifications

 - 7+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or a related GTM/Business Operations role.

 - Experience in fintech, SaaS, or a complex B2B enterprise sales motion.

 - Experience supporting Fund Administration, private markets, or another complex, services-driven revenue motion.

 - Hands-on Salesforce administration experience: you understand how data structure and process design impact downstream reporting and forecasting accuracy.

 - Experience owning end-to-end renewal and/or expansion workflows, including documentation, performance reporting, and cross-functional stakeholder alignment.

 - Experience managing forecasting, pipeline reporting, and recurring GTM operating cadences (QBRs, pipeline reviews, forecast calls).

 - Strong analytical skills, with proficiency in data and reporting tools (e.g., Salesforce reporting, Tableau, Looker, or advanced Google Sheets/Excel).

 - Proven ability to translate ambiguous business problems into clear processes, systems, and recommendations.

 - Strong stakeholder management and communication skills; comfort partnering with and influencing across teams, including establishing and enforcing rules of engagement.

 - AI fluency: you use AI tools like Claude to orchestrate multi-step workflows across two or more tools (e.g., CRM, spreadsheets, reporting/BI tools) producing reusable, structured outputs. You can describe at least one recurring revenue process you’ve redesigned around AI-assisted execution and speak to its team-level impact (e.g., reduced reporting turnaround, improved forecast accuracy, faster pipeline prep).

Nice to have:

 - 

 - Experience with GTM tooling such as Gong, Outreach, Apollo, or Clay.

If you’re energized by high standards, rapid growth, and the opportunity to help define a category at a pivotal moment, come join us!

Juniper Square offers employees a variety of ways to work, ranging from a fully remote experience to working full-time in one of our physical offices. We invest heavily in digital-first https://blog.junipersquare.com/juniper-square-ponders-future-of-office-with-digital-first-hybrid-workplace-strategy/ operations, allowing our teams to collaborate effectively across 27 U.S. states, 2 Canadian Provinces, India, Luxembourg, and England. We also have physical offices in San Francisco, New York City, Mumbai and Bangalore for employees who prefer to work in an office some or all of the time.




ABOUT YOUR ROLE

Juniper Square serves more than 2,200 GP customers, and most of them use a fraction of what we offer. We are standing up a dedicated expansion organization to change that, and we are looking for a Director of Expansion & Powered Admin Services to lead it.

The role carries two connected mandates. The first is the expansion motion across our installed base: cross-selling GPX products into GPX customers, into our Fund Administration client base, and Fund Administration into self-administered accounts. The second is Powered Admin Services, an emerging channel in which third-party fund administrators license or white-label Juniper Square technology, creating distribution to their GP clients at near-zero acquisition cost. Early partner conversations are underway; you will turn them into structured pilots and then into a repeatable channel.

Reporting to the Head of Sales, you will lead a team of dedicated expansion sellers, the first of whom is already in seat, and you will partner daily with our Fund Administration organization, Customer Success, Revenue Operations, Partnerships, and the asset-class sales leaders whose sellers hold commercial ownership of accounts in their first year.

This is a build role. The lead flow, the qualification bar, the whitespace and wallet-share analysis, the account-handoff enforcement, and the channel playbook do not yet exist in systematic form. Our working thesis is that a majority of expansion quota is attainable from strategic accounts we already serve. Nobody has tested that claim against data. You will.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

Carry the number

 - Own and deliver an expansion ARR quota as a working seller, not solely through a team. Run your own deals, in your own accounts, from day one.

 - Build and own the pipeline from the installed base rather than waiting for it to be routed to you.

Define the expansion motion

 - Come in and assess: what's actually there, what's sellable now, and where the real ceiling is. Turn the whitespace analysis into graded, prioritized account plans.

 - Build the wallet-share and whitespace program — categorize penetration targets, trust-building accounts, and structurally blocked accounts, and keep that intelligence current in Salesforce.

 - Set the qualification bar and build the plays per product, so the motion is repeatable rather than dependent on individual heroics.

 - Operationalize lead flow from the installed base: client signals surfaced by Fund Administration and Customer Success (fund launch plans, DDQ cycles, product usage) logged where sellers can act on them.

 - Define the adoption-first play: drive usage and training on technology clients already own as the door-opener, with paid expansion as the follow-on.

Scope Powered Admin Services

 - Size the market. How many fund administrators are realistic targets, what do they run today, and what would make them move.

 - Identify the buyer and the entry point. Run the first conversations and the first deals yourself.

 - Define what we're actually selling, in partnership with Product and Fund Administration leadership: the packaging, the boundaries, and what we will and won't support in a white-label arrangement.

 - Bring back an honest recommendation on whether this warrants a dedicated seller, and when.

Build the team

 - Partner with the seller already in seat to define the motion together, then hire and ramp behind it as volume justifies.

 - Own ramp plans, pipeline reviews, and MEDDPICC-based deal coaching. Define the book or territory split between sellers.

 - Run the volume analysis that justifies the next seat rather than assuming it.

Work the seams

 - Build a real operating cadence with Customer Success (Enterprise, Mid-Market & Growth), Fund Administration relationship managers, and the asset-class sales leaders whose sellers hold commercial ownership of accounts in their first year.

 - Enforce clean account-ownership rules: ownership windows, AE-to-expansion handoffs at the end of the window, the competitive-account exception path, and no passive compensation anywhere.

 - Feed Marketing the segments and signals that expansion campaigns need: DDQ plays, K-1 season plays, fund-launch triggers.

Report and refine

 - Own the expansion dashboard: pipeline created from the installed base, expansion ARR closed, attach rates by product, time-to-first-expansion, and adoption-to-paid conversion.

 - Bring model corrections to sales leadership quarterly — which routing rules are wrong, where the rules of engagement need amending, and whether the expansion and Powered Admin Services theses are holding.

Use AI as core infrastructure

 - Treat AI as central to how this function runs, not a side project. Build whitespace scoring, account-plan generation, and signal detection with our internal tooling rather than staffing them manually.

 - Redesign the work rather than adopt tools. The measure is workload that no longer requires a person, not software we've licensed.
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 8+ years in SaaS or fintech revenue roles with meaningful time in expansion or installed-base selling, and a track record of carrying and hitting a quota. We're open to candidates who've done this from inside Customer Success or from inside Sales — what matters is that you've owned a number.

 - Experience building a land-and-expand or installed-base motion, ideally more than once: usage-based lead scoring, adoption-first selling, and cross-functional selling through Customer Success and services teams.

 - People-leadership experience, including building a small team from zero, with the willingness to stay hands-on in deals while you do it.

 - Player-coach operating style. Roughly 10% strategy, 90% execution. You will be in accounts, not above them.

 - Comfortable in ambiguity. One of your two motions does not exist yet, and the other inherits rules that are still being reconciled. You'll need to run both while policy catches up.

 - Fluent in Salesforce as the operating system for the motion, and able to define requirements for RevOps and data tooling.

 - Demonstrated use of AI to create real efficiency in a revenue organization — workflow redesign, not tool adoption alone.

Strong plus

 - Experience selling technology to fund administrators, or from inside a company that does. A Customer Success or expansion background at a SaaS business serving fund administrators is close to the ideal profile here. We are not requiring it, and we will happily teach the Powered Admin Services side to a strong expansion leader.

 - Private markets experience, or experience selling financial technology at scale into institutional buyers. Credibility with a GP's CFO or controller goes a long way here.

 - Exposure to selling alongside a services organization, where margin, capacity, and delivery constraints shape the deal.

 - Experience standing up a white-label, OEM, or powered-by partnership motion.
   
   


COMPENSATION

Compensation for this position includes a base salary, commission, equity, and a variety of benefits. The U.S. base salary range for this role is $160,000 - $200,000. Actual base salaries will be based on candidate-specific factors, including experience, skillset, and location, and local minimum pay requirements as applicable.



Benefits include:

 - Health, dental, and vision care for you and your family

 - Life insurance

 - Mental wellness coverage

 - Fertility and growing family support

 - Flex Time Off in addition to company-paid holidays

 - Paid family leave, medical leave, and bereavement leave policies

 - Retirement saving plans

 - Allowance to customize your work and technology setup at home

 - Annual professional development stipend

Reporting to the VP of Total Rewards & People Operations, you’ll partner with Finance, FP&A, Talent Acquisition, and People Business Partners to keep our pay programs market-competitive, internally equitable, and built to scale. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role for someone with deep compensation and equity experience who can add value from day one — owning market pricing, the annual rewards cycle, bonus programs, and equity strategy while giving recruiters and leaders clear, data-backed recommendations. Our Senior Benefits & People Programs Manager serves as your backup on compensation and equity operations.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own market pricing and band builds across levels, job families, and geographies (U.S., Canada, India, UK), maintaining the Jobs Table as the source of truth and keeping systems in sync.

 - Own the quarterly grant cycles submitted for Board approval, reconcile equity data across Shareworks, HiBob, and Pave, and lead employee equity education.

 - Use structured candidate compensation data from Ashby to track where we win and lose on pay and flag when a band needs to be revisited, and support pay equity reviews to keep posted pay ranges current.

 - 7+ years of compensation experience, ideally within a SaaS or technology company operating across multiple geographies.

 - Experience administering bonus and variable pay plans and running compensation cycles in a platform such as Pave, with advanced spreadsheet and HRIS data modeling skills.
